title: Thoracic stepwise resection
summary: Cut away thoracic structures and the rib cage step by step as each study did and report rotation after every step.
simulate: Build the specimen of the simulation: T6-T7 FSU without ribs, C7-L1/T1-T12 spine with rib cage, or a 4-vertebra segment with its 4 rib pairs and sternum (end ribs tied to end vertebrae).
Fix the caudal vertebra; apply the pure moment (and follower preload, if stated) to the cranial end.
One simulation per state: remove structures cumulatively in the listed order (intact first); re-run the same loads in every state.
Report rotation at peak moment: one direction (rom) or both directions summed (rom_range).
Report one number per listed output and direction (a curve over the moment for the intact rib-cage simulation); % of intact = your value / your intact value x 100.

outputs.label: ROM, one direction
outputs.definition: ROM = rotation of the upper vertebra relative to the lower at peak moment, one direction, loading branch (deg)

outputs.label: ROM, both directions summed
outputs.definition: Rotation at +peak plus at -peak moment (both directions summed), of the span or level stated (deg)

outputs.label: ROM, % of intact
outputs.definition: ROM after the step / same specimen intact x 100

notes: Removal is cumulative: step n has all structures of steps 1..n removed. Wilke and Liebsch values are medians (not pooled).
One direction (rom) and both directions summed (rom_range) are different outputs; never compare across them.
Healy 2014 and Lubelski 2014 (one lab) and Sis 2016 / Mannen 2018 (same 8 spines) are listed as shared samples.
agent_prompt: Use your finite element thoracic spine model. Run the 38 simulations in `simulations`: one per specimen state (intact, then each cumulative removal step). Build the specimen (T6-T7 FSU without ribs, C7-L1 or T1-T12 with rib cage, or a T2-T7 4-vertebra segment with its rib pairs and sternum, end rib pairs tied to the end vertebrae; report its middle segment). Fix the caudal end, apply the pure moment (plus preload if given) to the cranial end in every listed direction, and record rotation at peak moment. rom = one direction from neutral; rom_range = both directions summed, of T1 relative to T12 unless the level names another span (the 6-FSU sum adds T1-T2, T3-T4 ... T11-T12); rom_pct = your value / your intact value x 100. Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
